rationale: This is essentially the product of two heavily documented anomalies (net payout yield and profitability/gross-profitability), and because both legs are non-negative ranks the "interaction" is monotone in each argument, making it a near-linear composite of known factors rather than a state-dependent effect — and its low tail conflates "uninformative" cases with genuine sell signals.

The soft cash-burn gate on gross issuance is a defensible refinement of the external-financing anomaly with sign and expression consistent, though the unranked, highly skewed raw issuance leg risks outlier domination and the cash-flow gate is partly a distress/profitability proxy that FF5 may absorb.

This is a direct rediscovery of the intersection of two canonical anomalies (Sloan accruals and share-issuance/composite-issuance), combined as a monotone rank product that adds no genuine conditioning beyond stacking two same-signed effects.

The signed strain score (leverage rank minus cash-flow rank) genuinely flips the interpretation of net debt flow across states and the expected negative sign is internally consistent for all four quadrants, with the main caveat that the signal collapses toward zero for mid-strain firms so extremes will drive the sort.

Conditioning buybacks on a multi-year cash-flow trend rather than a level is a reasonable and not-quite-standard refinement, but the mass of zero-repurchase firms creates a degenerate, tie-heavy low leg and the 5-year trend window will cost coverage, so the short side may be poorly identified.

Internally inconsistent: because both legs are non-negative ranks, dividend cuts by cash-rich and cash-poor firms both map near zero, so the expression cannot deliver the claimed sign flip for cuts and instead just reproduces a monotone dividend-increase × cash-conversion composite of known effects.
